Interface Inventory

All Known Subinterfaces:
EntityInventory, EntityInventory.Mutable, EquipmentInventorySection, EquipmentInventorySection.Mutable, Hotbar, Hotbar.Mutable, Inventory.Mutable, InventoryGrid, InventoryGrid.Mutable, InventorySection, InventoryView<Self>, InventoryView.Changing<Muta,Self>, InventoryView.Mutable<Self,Change>, PlayerCraftingInventory<Self>, PlayerCraftingInventory.Mutable, PlayerInventory<Self>, PlayerInventory.Changing, PlayerInventory.Mutable, PlayerMainInventory, PlayerMainInventory.Mutable, Slot<Self>, Slot.Changing, Slot.Mutable
public interface Inventory
A collection of slots is known as an inventory. This is not to be confused with what the client can interact with see InventoryView for that. As this is a collection of slots, this inventory can be virtual such as EntityInventory's equipment slots and held item. Any interaction done through this interface will affect all slots, as such the following example that will clear the connection's inventory 

   Connection.Mutable connection;
   connection.inventory().query(new QueryViaNotEmpty()).clear()

    • query

      @NotNull @CheckReturnValue @NotNull Optional<? extends Inventory> query(@NotNull @NotNull InventoryQuery query)
      The ability to query the inventory using an InventoryQuery. Queries are cached meaning that common queries should produce results quickly. The amount of queries stored varies depending on the inventory implementation. Run InventoryQuery.query(Inventory) to run without caching result
      Parameters:
      query - the query to run
      Returns:
      An optional inventory. If the result of the query has no slots then will return Optional.empty(). If a single slot is found then the optional will be present with the slot implementation however if more then one slot is found then an inventory containing just the slots that match the query will be returned
